title: A Bad Seance
subtitle: They lift chairs, smash furniture, and jump out of walls. And there's nothing you can do to stop them.

items.text: A Bad Seance

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: ... Isolde? Isolde!

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: My God, she passed out again!
People gather around in a loose circle, wringing their hands but offering little help, knowing there is little they can do besides making a spectacle of their compassion.

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: She must have smelling salts on her. Find them ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What is going on?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Make way, make way! Let me see ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Kakania! People, make way for the doctor!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Isolde, can you hear me? Oh no, it's a seizure. She's going to bite herself.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Get a stick! Heinrich, do you have any props she can bite ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: *panting* Doctor! Help ... Please help me ... They are here! The paintings ... They are here!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: D**n it! She can't wait ... Isolde, open your mouth ... Oof!

items.speaker: Guest I
items.text: Doctor! Your hand is bleeding from the bite!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's okay! What happened just now? She was fine when I left ten minutes ago.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: I ... don't know! We finished reciting Siegmund's poem ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... Siegmund? Oh, you mean Theophil. I see what's going on here. You've aroused her trauma.

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: You shouldn't have invited her to her brother's exhibition, Heinrich! And you even read his death notice in public! You should have known it would upset her!

items.speaker: Guest II
items.text: He was the only family she had left!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: *gasps* I did not ... I thought she had completely recovered.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... What?

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: She should have recovered from the electroshock therapy.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: What kind of nonsense is that? Dr. Schwartz is a liar without a conscience! He takes pleasure in the pain of his patients!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I know how he managed to fool the Medical Association ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Those rich morons don't care about the patients at all. Soon as you mention fancy words like "advanced" or "science," they'll throw their wallets at you as if they'll be left behind by the times.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: They're all blinded by the shining glamor of "progressivism," and they even scoff at psychoanalysis, the real meaningful discovery of the era ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Ahh!
A piercing scream silences her arguments.

The screaming woman, drenched in sweat, sees the framed painting turn into a bone saw aimed at cutting open her skull, where most certainly the syrup in her brain would diffuse like milk poured into a cup of tea.
How adorable—an almost delightful thought ... But, but ...
What if it's like the oil paint on this canvas? Or like a teacup? Like a neat triangle? Like a square, like a square, like a square, like a circle—

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: No! Theophil!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: ... Get away from me!
The electric lights go out, and a series of candles ignite simultaneously.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Haha, hahaha! Look at the ring, Theophil. It's so beautiful ...
In the candlelight, Isolde's face is deathly pale.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: *sobs* No, this was my fault ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Yes, yes, I will do better. I can do this! I can still sing ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Ugh ... Isolde?
The woman pulls Kakania down by her collar.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Please look at me, Doctor! Help me? Please help me!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I will, Isolde. Now let go of me first.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Oh no. It's a seance! But Ms. Tosca only does it before a performance.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Of course it turned out this way. She's lost control. She summoned evil spirits this time, not the good ones!

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: No, no! Get away, get away!
Kakania breaks free from her grip and follows Isolde's distant gaze.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: She's afraid of the paintings! Oh, poor girl. It's her brother's paintings ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Ugh!

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Ms. Kakania, watch out!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Heinrich, give me a hand!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Draw the ghosts away, by whatever means!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Alright. You're safe now, Isolde. Now, feel the pressure of my hands.
The wandering spirits busy themselves in entangling the unfortunate gentleman. Kakania, catching her breath, gently clasps her hands over Isolde's ears.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The pressure will remind you of some things. They'll enter your mind slowly and steadily, and they won't hurt you ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: *deep breath*

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Good, that's it.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: When I release the pressure, open your eyes slowly. Those things will fall softly to the ground, like feathers. Now grab them gently ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Now tell me, what did you see? What happened?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: *pants* Ugh ...
The woman clenches her teeth, struggling to push out her gritted words.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Ugh ... Dr. Schwartz told me that humans are rational and we should be able to control ourselves completely. But I failed. The Dittarsdorfs can't afford another lunatic like me.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I will be abandoned by the audience, by everyone!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: No! You are not them, Isolde. As long as you receive proper treatment in the hospital ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Please don't, please! I am cured ... The shock therapy worked well, very well!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Isolde ...

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: No, I mustn't act like mother or Theophil ... The Dittarsdorfs can't bear ... The opera can't bear ...
Still murmuring, her breathing gradually evens out.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Heinrich, please take Ms. Dittarsdorf to get some rest.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: I will.
The gentleman barks a command to the guests gathered around and moves to help the girl into the backstage.
Kakania rises, rushing to the door of the Secession Building like a gust of wind.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: What about you, doctor? Where are you going?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'm going to get that d****d Schwartz!
Her green figure swiftly disappears beneath the doorway.
But before the door can close, a hand halts its motion.

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Kakania ... Hmm? You are from the Foundation, and ...

items.speaker: Heinrich
items.text: Angelotti, and the Unknown Lady?
TO BE CONTINUED…
